output.text: When translating this invented poem, we chose to keep a pocket of rain—because it conveys portable sadness, a quiet weight carried through the day. We kept the image, letting the metaphor of rain in a pocket linger, vivid and intimate. Yet we lost the rhyme, as forcing a matching rhyme would have made the sentence awkward and strained. The rhythm faltered, the meaning blurred. In this case, preserving the image mattered more than perfect meter. The pocket of rain remains, a small, damp truth. It holds sorrow not as a storm, but as something small and carried. We kept the image, lost the rhyme, and found a deeper resonance.
